### Observed differences

- A01 was not observed in any of the 200 earlier traces; in the later window it runs exactly once in every trace (200 of 200), never repeated, and typically within the first third of the case (median relative position 0.2, mean about 0.29). [OCC001, POS001]
- Earlier, A02 always ran without A01; later, A01 and A02 occur together in 100 of 100 traces, always with A02 first. A01 also co-occurs with A03, A04, A06, A07 and A10 in the later window whenever those run, preceding A03, A06, A07 and A10 in about 90–97 in 100 of those joint cases; with A04 the order is mixed (A01 first in about 55 in 100, A04 first in about 45). [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL007]
- The flow into A01 is new: earlier, about 86 in 100 of A02's outgoing transitions went straight to A04 (with small shares to A07, A10, A05 and A03); later, about 54 in 100 go to A01 and about 44 directly to A04. A04, which never led to A01 earlier, now sends about 39 in 100 of its outgoing transitions there, and A01 in turn feeds mainly A04 (about 46 in 100), A07 (17), A03 (16) and A10 (10). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR004]
- A09 is gone from the later window: it ran in 90 of 200 earlier traces (about 45 in 100), always as the final event (mean relative position about 1.0, with only one outgoing transition ever observed), and was reached from A06 in 100 of 100 of that activity's outgoing transitions. Later, no trace contains A09; A06 itself now sits at the end of the case (mean relative position about 0.99, up from about 0.80) and shows only 3 observed outgoing transitions (two to A01, one to A04), so its new successors rest on very few observations. [OCC007, POS006, DIR006, DIR009, POS004]
- A09's earlier relations confirm that terminal role: it co-occurred with A02, A03, A04, A06 and A10 in about 45 in 100 earlier traces, always after them, and never with A07 (the two were alternatives); later it co-occurs with nothing. [REL006, REL011, REL016, REL020, REL023, REL025, REL027]
- Downstream activities now occur about one event position later: A03's mean relative position moved from about 0.51 to 0.68, A10's from 0.46 to 0.68, A04's from 0.24 to 0.31, and the spacing from A02 to A03, A06, A07 and A10 grew by about one step (A02-to-A06 pairs at lag 4 in about 99 of 100 earlier cases versus lag 5 in about 97 of 100 later pairs). These are event positions, not clock times. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS007, LAG001, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005]
- Outside these points behaviour is stable: participation of A03, A05, A06, A07, A08, A10 and A11 shifted by at most about 2–3 in 100 (for example A03 from 45 to about 48 in 100), a difference random re-splits typically produce. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC008, OCC009]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a structural restructuring with two facets: A01 was added as a new, always-executed early step, and A09 was dropped from the end of the process. In the later window A01 runs once per case after A02, receives about half of A02's outgoing flow (which earlier went almost entirely straight to A04) plus about four in ten of A04's outgoing transitions, and precedes the downstream activities A03, A04, A06, A07 and A10; A09, previously the final step after A06 in about 45 in 100 cases, is no longer observed, leaving A06 itself to end that branch. [OCC001, OCC007, DIR002, DIR004, DIR006, REL001, REL003]

The support is direct and consistent: both participation flips (0 to 200 of 200 traces for A01; 90 to 0 of 200 for A09) exceed all 200 random re-splits, the relational items show A01 now co-occurring with every other activity and A09 with none, the successor profiles of A02, A04 and A06 changed accordingly, and the one-step position and lag shifts downstream corroborate an insertion near the start of the case. [OCC001, OCC007, POS001, POS006, REL001, REL006, LAG003]

Limitations: event positions cannot pin down A01's exact placement, since A01 precedes A04 in about 55 in 100 later traces but follows it in about 45, so the new routing around A01 varies and cannot be fully resolved; and A09's absence strictly means only that it was not observed in 200 later traces, so an extremely rare residual path cannot be excluded. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the finer rerouting shares around A01 (such as the 54-to-44 split of A02's outgoing flow) are partly sampling variation between the two windows. [REL003, DIR002]

Other differences: participation and ordering among the remaining activities (A03, A05, A06, A07, A08, A10, A11) moved only within about 2–3 in 100, at the level random re-splits produce, and a few small lag or direction shifts (for example between A03 and A04, or A10 and A04) rest on fewer than ten observations and are too weak to interpret. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC008, OCC009, REL013, LAG006, LAG016]
